premise: I drained my $110,000 nursing pension to buy a derelict vineyard with my brother‑in‑law, who signed a notarized 40% equity stake and a lifetime supply of estate wines; when a wine conglomerate bid $950,000 for the brand and grapes, he forged a dissolution, sold everything, and handed me a $6,000 “gratitude” bottle. I recovered our contract from a sealed barrel, proved the forgery, and now own “Grapes of Wrath Vineyard,” where he crushes grapes in a shirt reading “Crushed Trust” and every wine label prints his fraud case number.
